kind: bounded source audit; not product correctness or implementation authorization

requirement.title: top-k values and indices
requirement.domain: k=1/configured/E; stable tie order; NaN policy explicit; tail and empty rejected domain
requirement.oracle: stable scalar ordering; separate value and selection arrays

facts: Public Vulkan Program/Results/Recorder already express multiple output tensors; private PlanStep/RegionNode and their validation still accept only one output.
Original ggml_top_k explicitly does not promise output order; ggml_argsort_top_k uses a separate full-sort path.

Both original argsort shaders compare only floating values and reverse ascending results for DESC. Two equal values therefore give [1,0] for DESC rather than stable [0,1]; this is a source-derived counterexample, not a GPU run.
Both argsort implementations use a bitonic network: retain topology, barriers, dispatch and scratch ownership while adapting the comparison semantics.
GET_ROWS has an original I32 shader with uint input, temporary and output, enabling raw 32-bit payload gathering without arithmetic conversion.

ggml_backend_tensor_alloc explicitly asserts view_src == NULL. Published index/value views need an actual allocation-compatible materialization or an explicitly correct owner binding; a view cannot simply be imported as a fresh independent tensor.

A TopK graph needs more metadata nodes than the existing three-per-operation formula. The finite fix must account for actual reshape/view/cont/sort/gather nodes and overflow before native metadata construction.
cost: Full sort O(rows * padded_width * log^2(width)); full index storage, long-row ivec2 scratch, raw-value gather, any layout and published-view copies must be counted.
next_action: Finish and archive the live immutable delivery queue, publish finite Y21-Y24 to current owner cards, then implement and qualify. Source investigation stops here.
